purpose: Guide an operating plan, roadmap, or vision narrative that links direction, evidence, initiatives, goals, and resource choices.

ordered_sections.title: Document control
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify the plan mode, horizon, owner, version, and approval status.

ordered_sections.title: Purpose, mission, and vision
ordered_sections.purpose: State the team's purpose and the direction this plan supports.

ordered_sections.title: Background and operating context
ordered_sections.purpose: Give an unfamiliar reader the context needed to assess the plan.

ordered_sections.title: Financial or business summary
ordered_sections.purpose: Summarize business performance and economics when they affect the decision.

ordered_sections.title: Current situation and learnings
ordered_sections.purpose: Compare current performance with relevant expectations and explain highlights, misses, and lessons.

ordered_sections.title: Goals and operating mental model
ordered_sections.purpose: Define measurable outcomes and the model used to organize the plan.

ordered_sections.title: Strategy portfolio and themes
ordered_sections.purpose: Describe the limited set of strategic choices and how the themes relate.

ordered_sections.title: Key initiatives and plans
ordered_sections.purpose: Connect each priority to a customer or business problem, mechanism, measure, and dependency.

ordered_sections.title: Funding, headcount, and resource elasticity
ordered_sections.purpose: Show resource choices and the outcomes gained or lost when funding is decision-relevant.

ordered_sections.title: Executive diligence FAQ
ordered_sections.purpose: Address difficult choices, underexamined risks, misses, opportunities, and tradeoffs.

ordered_sections.title: Tenets
ordered_sections.purpose: Record prioritized principles that resolve recurring choices when the plan needs them.

ordered_sections.title: Evidence appendices and data tables
ordered_sections.purpose: Provide supporting detail without moving essential reasoning out of the main narrative.

narrative_rules: State the purpose, recommendation, and material planning choice near the beginning.
Connect mission to tenets, themes, initiatives, goals, and resource choices.
For context, move from observed state to evidence, interpretation, and planning implication.
For a performance gap, identify the result, comparator, gap, and consequence.
For a commitment, identify the owner, action, mechanism, outcome, measure, and dependency.
For a strategic bet, distinguish the assumption, supporting evidence, test, decision gate, and protection.
For an enabler, explain the constraint, affected themes, work, adoption or reliability outcome, and owner.
Be direct about misses, uncertainty, and strategic tradeoffs.
Explain customer or business consequence before implementation detail.
Cover a small set of material topics with sufficient depth instead of listing many thin themes.
Preserve executive argument density while using shorter sentences when a language overlay requires it.
evidence_rules: Keep actuals, forecasts, assumptions, proposed targets, approved targets, and commitments distinct.
For every material measure, record its definition, population, period, unit, comparator, source, and caveat.
Align periods, populations, regions, and units before making a comparison.
A highlight must explain the result, its importance or comparison, the causal mechanism, and how the learning will be used.
A lowlight must explain the affected result, impact, root cause or uncertainty, corrective mechanism, owner, timing, and prevention or inspection method.

Before drafting, inventory every material source fact, value, qualifier, population, period, owner, timing, resource, dependency, gate, caveat, and evidence state in the server-provided source-unit ledger.

A source unit counts as covered only when an exact draft excerpt preserves all of its material anchors; record an explicit scope, duplication, or relevance reason for each review unit that is omitted.

Register every material statement in the claim ledger and keep semantic claim type separate from evidence state; missions, recommendations, decision gates, and dependencies are not targets or commitments.
Keep open dependencies, questions, proposals, and forecasts at their source modality; do not convert them into requirements or approval prerequisites.
Do not invent document-control metadata. If a required control field has no authoritative value, write ‘Not provided’ rather than creating a version, date, owner, approval, or classification.
Do not present an unexplained target or an invented baseline as established evidence.
terminology_rules: Use one stable term for each goal, theme, initiative, metric, and planning state.
Classify every theme as a funnel stage, strategic bet, or horizontal enabler.
Use visible labels for any evidence state that is not an actual.
Expand acronyms at first use unless the authoritative audience glossary marks them as universally understood.
formatting_rules: Keep essential reasoning in the main narrative and use appendices only for support.
Use tables for aligned comparisons, resource scenarios, and dense evidence when prose would obscure the relationship.
Number prioritized items and FAQ entries.
Apply the current organization template before default page and typography guidance.
Keep headings with their following content and include required page, title, and confidentiality controls.
hard_fail_rules: Block publication when any theme is disconnected from goals, initiatives, or the rest of the strategy.
Block publication when a baseline is fabricated or a target lacks explanation and approval state.
Block publication when a resource request omits the customer or business consequence.
Block publication when evidence is fabricated, untraceable, mislabeled, or missing critical population or period context.
Block publication when body text and tables conflict or another material contradiction remains unresolved.
Block publication when a date, owner, target, fact, or commitment is introduced without authority.
Block publication when required overview context is absent without an approved exception.
Block publication when source-specific sample facts appear in a new artifact.
Block publication when repair changes a decision, requirement, or protected fact.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.

source_manifest.reference: Supplied OP, roadmap, and vision reference
